thread:
Tara (Design): Quick pulse check: new compact roles layout where the left column shows role + up to 3 task-based chips (verb labels), with an affordance to expand full permission grid. Prototype: https://staging.redwood.design/compact-v2 :sparkles:
Evan (PM): Love the idea. Two product asks: 1) make default invite role explicit in the invite modal, 2) SSO toggle copy should clarify when SSO is enforced org-wide vs optional.
Rina (Frontend): Accessibility nits: chips must be real buttons with aria-pressed and explicit aria-labels. Avoid color-only states; add an indicator icon and text. For virtualized lists, preserve expansion state across virtualization.
Omar (UX Research): In 8 quick interviews, admins expected verbs like "Remove members" instead of vague labels. They also wanted a persistent audit link from the role row (not buried in details).
Jules (Accessibility): Contrast check: our current neutral-400 chips fail 3:1 for small text. We need 4.5:1 for normal text. Suggest neutral-700 for inactive and accent-600 for active. Also ensure focus ring is at least 3px and visible on high-contrast themes.
Tara (Design): Microcopy ideas: replace "Admin" with task labels. For invite modal show a small line: "Default role assigned to new invites: <Role Name> — change". For SSO: label: "Require SSO for all org logins" with a tooltip: "When on, sign-in via email/password is disabled for this org."
Evan (PM): For audit navigation, propose a keyboard shortcut: focus role > press "." (period) then "a" to open audit filtered by that role. Also the audit panel should show a top breadcrumb: "Showing changes for role: <Role>". Ensure deep-linking so we can link into the audit view.
Rina (Frontend): Implementation note: API should return priority_permissions in the roles list to avoid client recompute for large orgs. Also add a flag in the role object: "expanded_by_default": false so migration is smoother.
Omar (UX Research): Proposed test tasks: locate who can "manage billing", invite a new user with a custom role, find the most recent permission change for a role. Include keyboard-only and NVDA/VoiceOver participants.
Jules (Accessibility): Keyboard details: expansion chevron must be reachable by tab and have aria-controls linking to the expanded grid. When expanded, focus should go to the first editable permission. Announce via aria-live: "Expanded permissions for role X".
Tara (Design): Layout question: do we show priority chips for the "Default role" (the org default for invites)? If yes, we should visually mark it as default (chip with star). Thoughts?
Evan (PM): Yes, show default badge. In the invite flow we also need a clear callout when the inviter overrides defaults. Copy: "This invite will assign role: <Role>. Change default".
Rina (Frontend): CSS prototype for accessible focus + chips:
```css
.role-row:focus-within { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.priority-chip { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding:6px 8px; border-radius:8px; }
.priority-chip[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--accent-subtle); }
.priority-chip .label { font-weight:600; }
```
Rina (Frontend): We'll map tokens to hex values that meet contrast. Also will add aria-live notifications.
Omar (UX Research): Metrics to capture: expand_role (role_id), open_audit_from_role (role_id), override_default_role (user_id). Helps validate scanning gains.
Tara (Design): Action items:
- @Rina: implement chip semantics + focus styles + aria-live (ETA Tue)
- @Jules: produce contrast token suggestions and keyboard focus spec (ETA Mon)
- @Evan: finalize invite modal copy + SSO toggle tooltip copy (ETA Wed)
- @Omar: draft test script and recruit 6 admins + 3 screen reader users (ETA Thu)
- @Tara: update mockups with default-role badge + audit shortcut hint (ETA Mon)
